title.narrative: Togo Essential Quality Health Services For Universal Health Coverage Project

description.narrative: The parent project, Togo Essential Quality Health Services for Universal Health Coverage Project, with a total financing of US$70 million equivalent, was approved on March 11, 2021, and became effective on August 5, 2021, with a closing date of April 30, 2026. The proposed Additional Financing (AF) will add to the existing operation, with revisions planned to broaden the range of activities and address identified challenges to help the project achieve its development objective. This AF will provide a total financing of US$81 million equivalent (US$70 million - IDA credit, US$10 million - Health System Transformation and Resilience Multi-Donor Trust Fund, and US$1 million grant - Health Emergency Preparedness and Response Multi-Donor Trust Fund) to address funding gaps, cost overruns, and supports new activities to improve health service delivery, digitalization, and emergency preparedness. This AF aims to expand the scope of the parent project to address critical gaps in the supply and demand of quality health and nutrition services, with a large focus on Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health and Nutrition (RMNCAH+N) particularly as partner resources in Togo are declining. The operation will also address cost overruns due to underestimated construction and renovation costs for primary healthcare facilities. A Level II restructuring of the project is also planned, which will include: (i) the addition of new activities under Components 1 and 3; (ii) revisions to the results framework and Performance-Based Conditions (PBCs) to more accurately capture implementation progress and reflect the expanded scope; (iii) revisions to the implementation arrangements with the shift from a Presidential to a Parliamentary system in Togo in March 2024; and (iv) an extension of the project's closing date for the original financing to December 31, 2027 and for the AF to April 30, 2029, to allow adequate time for the completion of planned activities. All revisions are consistent with the World Bank's Country Partnership Framework (CPF) for Togo for FY25–FY29 (Report No. 185419-TG) discussed by the Executive Directors on May 23, 2024, and the Government's Prevention and Resilience Allocation (PRA) Strategy and Monitoring Framework, which was approved in May 2024, where this proposed AF is aligned with High-Level Outcome 2 (HLO2, Improving Human Capital), which will support Togo's progress toward UHC by improving access to health facilities, increasing human resources in the health sector, and fostering a higher coverage of the NSHI Scheme. It is also aligned with the Corporate Scorecard Commitment on crisis preparedness and health emergency preparedness and response.The Additional Financing is structured around the same complementary components and sub-components, except in Component 1 with the addition of two sub-components; one on Strengthening health emergency preparedness and response and the second on Strengthening service delivery and system readiness through innovations. The five components are as follows: (a) Component 1: Increasing the demand for and supply of quality health and nutrition services, which is partly implemented through PBCs to improve the quality of health services; (b) Component 2: Bringing health facilities and services closer to households, which aims to build 160 PHC facilities, renovate 150 PHC facilities, and equip them; (c) Component 3: Strengthening the NSHI, which aims to lay the foundations for UHC; (d) Component 4: Improved stewardship, oversight, and management, which helps ensure proper management of project activities; and (e) Component 5: Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC), which allows the rapid reallocation of project resources in response to a natural and manmade disaster that has caused, or is likely to imminently cause, significant adverse economic and/or social impacts. Under the parent project, the Project Coordination Unit (PCU) is under the Office of the President with two Project Implementation Units (PIUs): one at the Ministry of Health and Public Hygiene and one at the Institute of National Health Insurance (Institut National de l’Assurance Maladie, INAM) at the Ministry of Access to Care and Universal Health Coverage. Due to a governmental reform, the PCU is now under the Office of the President of the Council and the reform in the health sector has merged the two ministries into a single entity: the Ministry of Health, Public Hygiene, Universal Health Coverage, and Insurances (MoH-UHC).
To improve the provision of essential health and nutrition services and quality of care for pregnant women, children and vulnerable populations

condition.narrative: Schedule 2-I. A.1.(a). No later than six (6) months after the Project Effective Date, the Recipient shall establish within theOffice of the President, and thereafter maintain, throughout Project implementation, a project coordination unit with terms ofreference, composition and resources acceptable to the Association (“Project Coordination Unit” or “PCU”).

Schedule 2-I. B.1. No later than six (6) months after the Effective Date, the Recipient shall adopt and thereafter implement theProject in accordance with the project implementation manual (“Project Implementation Manual” or “PIM”), with terms and conditionssatisfactory to the Association.

Schedule 2-I. C.3. For purposes of the implementation Parts 1.1, 1.2 and 1.4, the Recipient, through the Ministry of Health, PublicHygiene and Universal Access to Care, shall enter into an agreement (“Subsidiary Agreement”) with the Togo Social Health InsuranceAgency (“TSHIA”), in form and substance acceptable to the Association.

Schedule 2-I. D.(b).(i). For purposes of counter verification of the payments under the Eligible Expenditures for the PBCs underPart 1.1, 1.2 and 1.4 of the Project, the TSHIA shall:(i) No later than twelve (12) months after the Effective Date, and with theapproval of the PCU, contract and maintain throughout Project implementation pursuant to the Procurement Regulations and inaccordance with terms of reference satisfactory to the Association, one or more Independent Counter-Verification Agency (ICVA),with experience and qualifications in the health and social sectors acceptable to the Association, to conduct independentthird-party counter-verifications, in compliance with the verification protocols included in the PIM.

Schedule 2-I.D.(c) (i) for purposes of counter verification of the payments for the Eligible Expenditures for the PBCs under Part1.3 of the Project, the Ministry of Health, Public Hygiene and Universal Access to Care:(i) No later than six (6) months after theEffective Date, and with the approval of the PCU, contract and maintain throughout Project implementation pursuant to theProcurement Regulations and in accordance with terms of reference satisfactory to the Association, one or more IndependentCounter-Verification Agency (ICVA), with experience and qualifications in the health and social sectors acceptable to theAssociation, to conduct independent third-party counter-verifications, in compliance with the verification protocols included inthe PIM.

Schedule 2-IV. No later than six (6) months after the Effective Date, the Recipient shall provide evidence to the Association,acceptable to the Association of: (a) the issuance and approval of a Presidential Decree creating the integrated national healthinsurance entity, “Togo Social Insurance Agency (“TSHIA”), which shall absorb the existing entities such as Institut Nationald’Assurance Maladie (“INAM”); and (b) the establishment of a PIU within the TSHIA, in a manner acceptable to the Association.
